newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary sees budget gap of 4.9 pct of GDP in 1998.
newsitem.headline: Hungary sees budget gap of 4.9 pct of GDP in 1998.

text.p: Hungary's government budget deficit target for 1998 is 4.9 percent of the gross domestic product (GDP), unchanged from the 1997 target, government spokesman Elemer Kiss said on Thursday.
The government on Thursday approved certain key figures of the 1998 budget draft.
"The budget planning for 1998 calculates with three to four percent GDP growth and 13.5 percent (average) inflation," Kiss told a news conference following the cabinet meeting.
Hungary's GDP is expected to rise by two to three percent this year, while the government forecasts inflation of between 17 and 19 percent, down from 23.6 percent in 1996.
He added that without debt service expenditures, the 1998 budget would post a surplus of two percent of the GDP.

Total expenditures are planned to increase by maximum 16 to 17 percent, while the real value of spending on agricultural development, public security and Hungary's integration into the western world should rise in line with GDP growth, Kiss said.
The real value of government investments should increase by 10 to 12 percent with a focus on investments in production, he added.
Kiss said that the 1998 budget targeted a current account deficit of $2.1 billion, compared with a projected $2 billion for this year.
The government budget will redistribute 46.6 percent of the GDP in 1998, down from a planned 49.3 percent in 1997 and 51 percent in 1996, he said.
Kiss added that the government did not plan any major changes on the revenue side of the budget compared with 1997.

He said the government would discuss budget plans again in two weeks, and the budget guidelines will be submitted to the parliament by the end of July, while the detailed budget will be submitted around the middle of September.
